annotation.authors_or_issuer: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Department of Transportation
key_provisions_or_claims: Aircraft must be registered with the FAA Registry by eligible owners (U.S. citizens, resident aliens, qualifying corporations) before operation.
Certificates of Aircraft Registration expire seven years after issue and can be renewed.
Section 47.14 requires manufacturer-issued serial numbers for unmanned aircraft with remote identification, unique to one registration.
Dealer's Aircraft Registration Certificates allow manufacturers and dealers to flight test and demonstrate aircraft.
Applicants must submit evidence of ownership, pay fees, and notify the Registry of changes in status.
annotation.summary_en: Title 14 CFR Part 47, FAA aircraft registration rules: eligibility, ownership evidence, registration numbers, fees, certificate duration and renewal, and dealer certificates. Only a passing provision (§47.14) addresses serial numbers for unmanned aircraft with remote identification; otherwise it is conventional manned-aircraft registration administration.
